explanation: This slide discusses two autosomal dominant disorders: Osteogenesis Imperfecta and Hereditary Spherocytosis. Osteogenesis Imperfecta causes weakened, brittle bones, and most cases result from mutations in genes required to synthesize type I collagen. Hereditary Spherocytosis is caused by a mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene, which causes red blood cells to become spherical, fragile, and easy to burst.

questions.q: What molecular defect is responsible for most cases of Osteogenesis Imperfecta?
opts: A mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene.
A lack of elastin in the blood.
Mutation in genes required for the synthesis of type I collagen.
Absence of the muscle protein dystrophin.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide states: 'Most cases are caused by mutation in genes required for the synthesis of type I collagen' under Osteogenesis Imperfecta.

questions.q: What is the cause and cellular phenotype of Hereditary Spherocytosis?
opts: Defective elastin gene; causes premature aging of skin.
Mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene; causes red blood cells to become spherical, fragile, and burst easily.
Lack of type I collagen; causes brittle bones.
Absence of clotting factors; causes failure to clot.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide states Hereditary Spherocytosis is 'Caused by a mutation in the ankyrin-1 gene' causing 'Red blood cells become spherical, are fragile, and burst easily'.
